conceptual assets.information: The two source operand values supplied for each multiply or divide operation; correct arithmetic behavior depends on their values. Their derived information can also be observed indirectly through the arithmetic result returned on res_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The operands can contain sensitive data and are captured or carried through the arithmetic datapaths and into the externally visible result (171-172, 212, 264-272, 325-329). Changing the captured operands or their arithmetic inputs changes the computed result (171-172, 212, 225-227, 264-272). The requested operation cannot produce its intended result without the operands, and the start-controlled capture paths can withhold their use (154-155, 170-172, 210-212, 261-272).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the returned result or alter or suppress operand capture so that private operands are exposed or the requested operation produces no valid result.

conceptual assets.information: The multiply, divide, or remainder value computed from the source operands and selected operation; the processor depends on it as the coprocessor's returned result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The computed value may contain sensitive operand-derived information and is exposed through res_o (319-329). The multiplier and divider result registers and result-selection logic can be altered to change the returned value (184, 208-215, 264-300, 319-329). The result is withheld as zero unless ctrl.out_en releases it, so corrupting the release path can block the required result (321-329). The cpu_trap input can terminate a busy operation before completion and allow an incomplete intermediate value to be released as the result (131-138, 319-329).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could tamper with intermediate arithmetic state or assert cpu_trap during a multi-cycle operation, causing an incorrect, exposed, or withheld result.

conceptual assets.information: The internal state, iteration count, output-release state, and signedness settings that determine whether a multiply or divide operation is running, how it progresses, and when its result is valid. Completion is reported through valid_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Unauthorized modification of the state, iteration counter, output-enable state, or signedness settings can change operation progress, operand interpretation, or result release (107-138, 148-151). The state transitions and counter determine whether the operation reaches completion and drives valid_o, so corrupting them can stall or disable the coprocessor (120-145). The integration-level cpu_trap behavior can force a busy operation to S_DONE before its normal iterations finish, producing incorrect output or terminating the operation (131-138).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the progress state or assert the trap control during execution to prevent completion or release an incorrectly interpreted result.

conceptual assets.information: The internally decoded decision that a valid multiply or divide command is accepted and that the corresponding datapath is started. It has no entry or exit port because it is generated from decoded instruction fields and only controls internal launch.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing valid_cmd or the mutually selected multiply and divide start controls can accept the wrong command, select the wrong datapath, or alter whether the operation starts (97-99, 120-125, 154-155). Suppressing these controls prevents the requested operation from being accepted or launched (120-125, 154-155).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the launch decision inactive or select the wrong arithmetic path so that a valid command is ignored or executed incorrectly.

considered, not kept.reason: The opcode and function fields only select the operation or result form, so Operation selectors (a) treats them as part of the operation rather than as a separate piece of information (97-99, 121, 148-155, 323-329).

considered, not kept.concept: Intermediate multiplier and divider working values

considered, not kept.reason: Clocks and resets are barred as conceptual assets because clk_i only times state updates and rstn_i only resets the internal state and datapath registers (30-31, 104-110, 164-169, 205-209, 253-260).
FAST_MUL_EN and DIVISION_EN are build-time generics that select generated hardware and cannot be changed or withheld at run time (25-26, 161-162, 192-193, 249-250, 305-306).
ctrl_i.cpu_trap is a processor context field used only to refine the progress-state transition, so it is not a separate conceptual asset of this unit (131-132).
